title: Arabic letter in a secret script, Ihnas, 9th c. (ÖNB P.Vindob. A. P. 11016)

documents.shelfmark: ÖNB Papyrussammlung, P.Vindob. A. P. 11016 recto, lines 1-11

plaintext.source: none found; ÖNB description: 'Inhalt unbekannt', unpublished

transcription.source: ÖNB IIIF DTL_4865249 canvas 1 at 636 px, line crops upscaled 3x
transcription.notes: Four readings (tr/reader1.md, second_reader.md, reader3.md, reader4.md); majority consensus in tr/consensus2.txt: 77 signs with a majority label, 9 wildcards. The measured length is that of draft 1.

system.summary: Right-to-left secret script of about 18 Greek/Coptic-like signs joined like Arabic, with an Arabic-looking word-final group and colon dividers; Karabacek (1894) took it for a substitution cipher of Arabic; system not established.
system.notes: The circle makes up about a quarter of the signs (null, vowel sign or alif?). The colon marks may be dividers or letter dots.

prior_solution.where: Karabacek, PERF Fuehrer (1894) p. 226 no. 844: claims a key, prints three sign groups with readings (one is line 1), no full reading; Bogensperger and Reinfandt, Tyche 34 (2019): the signs differ from the dinar numerals of A.P. 5584 and are unread.

tools: Arabic, vocalised Arabic, Coptic and Greek n-gram models

solution.what: ÖNB IIIF API back up; manifest DTL_4865249 and three 636x2464 views fetched, line crops upscaled 3x.
Compared the 11 lines with the Vienna numeral table A.P. 1255. Four sign assignments match reversed numerical order within each abjad tier. Applying the proposed key yields no continuous reading.

Word-order and continuous-span checks on all four reader-9 variants. No attested consecutive group pair. The seven-letter line 9 exact hit in variant C is equalled or exceeded in 164 of 999 within-line sign shuffles. See RESULT.md.

outcome.method_basis: The fold reproduces historical assignments but no independently verified sentence. The four reader-9 transcriptions yield no adjacent group pair attested in the documentary-letter corpus.
outcome.notes: The group on line 1 matches Karabacek’s printed example. The interpretation of the raised ring on line 4 remains uncertain.
